title: Senior Electrical Engineer – Southern Europe, RME Amazon Logistics
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s last-mile delivery network in Southern Europe is growing fast — and becoming increasingly electrified. From EV chargers to next-generation sorting technologies, our Delivery Stations (the final logistics hubs from which parcels are dispatched to customers’ doors) are evolving into highly technical environments that demand deep electrical expertise. Today, that expertise is fragmented across operational teams. We’re changing that by creating a dedicated regional electrical authority within the Reliability, Maintenance & Engineering (RME) Leadership Team for Amazon Logistics (our last-mile delivery division, operating 200+ stations across Europe).

As Senior Electrical Engineer for Southern Europe (France, Italy, Spain), you will be the single point of electrical expertise for our Delivery Station network across the region. This is a senior technical expert role at the leadership level: you won’t manage a team directly, but you will deliver results through others — upskilling field teams, shaping standards, and steering technology projects that will define what our sites look like three years from now.

This role is based in Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, or Milan, with approximately 20–25% travel across Southern Europe.


Key job responsibilities
• Define the electrical strategy for future Delivery Stations: Lead upstream electrical engineering for new site installations and technology deployments (including EV charging infrastructure), partnering with design, construction, and central engineering teams to ensure readiness from Day 1.
• Own the 3-year technology roadmap (electrical scope): Evaluate, validate, and prepare the reception of emerging technologies across the Southern Europe network, ensuring electrical systems are designed, specified, and commissioned to the highest safety and performance standards.
• Upskill field teams on electrical standards and processes: Design and deliver training programs for field engineers and technicians across three countries, building consistent electrical knowledge and standardised ways of working.
• Drive cross-regional knowledge sharing: Establish structured Best Practice and Lessons Learned mechanisms with counterparts in the UK and Central/Northern Europe, ensuring innovations scale across the European network while respecting local regulatory contexts.
• Contribute to RME Leadership Team priorities: As a member of the Reliability, Maintenance & Engineering Leadership Team, participate actively in strategic planning, talent bar-raising (conducting interviews to support the team’s significant growth in Europe), and safety governance.


About the team
We are the Reliability, Maintenance & Engineering (RME) team — the people who keep Amazon’s buildings, equipment, and technologies running every single day so Operations can deliver for customers. Our mission: shift from reactive maintenance to predictive intelligence, where systems help us identify issues and prescribe the fix before operations feel the impact. Amazon’s logistics network is growing more complex every year — shifting from mechanical systems to interconnected, AI-augmented digital systems — and we’re building the engineering capability to match.

Basic qualifications

- Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent technical discipline
- Significant experience in electrical engineering within industrial, logistics, or infrastructure environments
- Proven ability to manage complex technical projects across multiple sites and countries
- Experience influencing and delivering results through others without direct line management
- Fluent English (spoken and written); proficiency in at least one of French, Italian, or Spanish

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with EV charging infrastructure, high-voltage systems, or power distribution design
- Knowledge of European electrical regulations across multiple countries (NF C 15-100, CEI 64-8, REBT, etc.)
- Experience developing technical training programs or standards at scale
- Background in logistics, e-commerce, or high-throughput operational environments
- Lean, Six Sigma, or project management certification

title: Senior Software Engineer, Bottlerocket
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to join the Bottlerocket team, where you'll build and evolve a purpose-built Linux-based operating system for running containers. Bottlerocket is fully open source and powers container workloads across Amazon EKS, Amazon ECS, and bare-metal environments at massive scale.

As an L6 SDE on this team, you will own significant components of the OS, from system services and update mechanisms to security hardening and package management. You'll design solutions that balance reliability, security, and performance for millions of container hosts, while collaborating openly with the broader community. - Cross-team integration — Collaborate with internal and external partner teams to ensure Bottlerocket meets orchestrator requirements and customer needs.
- Operational excellence — Own the build and release pipeline (including Twoliter, the Bottlerocket build system), drive quality through automated testing, and support production rollouts.
- Mentorship & technical leadership — Raise the bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentoring junior engineers on systems programming best practices.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with open source tools and resources
- Experience in Linux/RHEL, or experience in Ubuntu/Solaris and experience with threat modeling and penetration testing

title: Systems Development Engineer II, AWS Cross Domain Services (CDS)
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Cross Domain Services team is seeking a Systems Development Engineer who is passionate about operational excellence. This engineer will help to operate and scale the services that connect AWS regions of differing security requirements.

An Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) is a collection of AWS regions provided for a customer with specific security requirements. The AWS Cross Domain Services team provides solutions for customers to move data between regions with differing security requirements. We are obsessed with earning and maintaining customer trust. AWS is building some of the largest and most complex distributed systems in the world and the AWS Cross Domain Services team is essential to AWS’s dedicated cloud expansion. title: Duales Studium - BWL
descriptionHtml:
Ein Job im Operations-Bereich bei Amazon versetzt dich ins Zentrum dessen, wie Dinge vom Klick bis zur Haustür gelangen. Du hilfst dabei, Systeme zu entwerfen, zu verbessern und zu betreiben, die Menschen, Produkte und Orte miteinander verbinden – und das in großem Maßstab. Du übernimmst früh Verantwortung, arbeitest eng mit Teams zusammen, um reale Herausforderungen zu lösen, und siehst die direkten Ergebnisse deiner Entscheidungen, wenn sie täglich bei den Kunden ankommen. Hier ist die Wirkung dessen, was du aufbaust, nicht abstrakt – sie ist sichtbar, unmittelbar und bedeutsam – und hält eine der komplexesten Betriebsorganisationen der Welt am Laufen. Hier nimmt deine Reise Gestalt an – durch Handeln, Verantwortung und die Möglichkeit, in viele Richtungen zu wachsen Dein Einstieg in die Führung - Das Duale Studium bei Amazon
- Studiengang: BWL / Logistikmanagement (B.A.)
- Studienpartner: IU Internationale Hochschule (30+ Standorte deutschlandweit)
- Programmbeginn: 1. August 2027
- Dauer: 3,5 Jahre
- Einsatzorte: mehr als 20 Amazon-Standorte in Deutschland (Fulfillment Center und Sort Center)
Das duale Studium bei Amazon ist ein strukturiertes Führungsentwicklungsprogramm, das dich Schritt für Schritt auf eine operative Führungsrolle vorbereitet. Wer das Programm erfolgreich abschließt, hat die Chance direkt eine Position als Area Manager:in in unserem Netzwerk zu bekommen - ohne weiteres Bewerbungsverfahren.
________________________________________
Drei Phasen auf dem Weg zur Führungskraft
Das Programm ist in drei aufeinander aufbauende Phasen gegliedert, die deinen Verantwortungsbereich kontinuierlich erweitern.
Phase 1 - Operative Grundlagen: Zunächst lernst du die operativen Abläufe im Fulfillment Center von Grund auf kennen, analysierst Kennzahlen und setzt eigenständig Projekte zur Prozessverbesserung um.
Phase 2 - Rotation & Führungsentwicklung: Anschließend rotierst du durch verschiedene operative Bereiche, übernimmst schrittweise Führungsaufgaben - von der Begleitung der Team Leads über Schichtplanung bis hin zur Personalsteuerung - und entwickelst ein Verständnis für bereichsübergreifende Zusammenhänge.
Phase 3 - Area-Manager-Niveau: In der Abschlussphase arbeitest du auf Area-Manager-Niveau: Du steuerst operative Kennzahlen, führst Teams eigenständig und trägst echte Verantwortung für deinen Bereich.

Das bieten wir dir
• Karriereperspektive: Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Programms wechselst du direkt in eine Area Manager Position im Amazon-Netzwerk - ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren
• Studienfinanzierung: Amazon übernimmt die Studiengebühren an der IU
• Mentoring: Strukturierte Begleitung durch Learning Manager:in und operative Führungskräfte
• Netzwerk: Zugang zu einem europaweiten Operations-Netzwerk
• Mobilität: Kostenloses Deutschlandticket
• Verpflegung: Bezuschusste Mahlzeiten am Standort
• Mitarbeitervorteile: Vielfältige Vorteile, wie ein Amazon Mitarbeiterrabatt
• Technologie: Arbeite täglich mit modernster Automatisierungs- und Robotiktechnologie

Key job responsibilities
• Analyse und Optimierung operativer Prozesse in Fulfillment- und Sortierbereichen
• Eigenständige Durchführung von Continuous Improvement Projekten mit messbaren Ergebnissen
• Übernahme von Führungsaufgaben im Rahmen von Lead-Rotationen (Schichtverantwortung, Teamsteuerung, KPI-Management)
• Mitarbeit an bereichsübergreifenden Projekten in den Bereichen Arbeitssicherheit, Prozessoptimierung, Personalwesen und Technik
• Vorbereitung auf die eigenständige Steuerung eines operativen Bereichs als Area Manager:in
• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit einem internationalen Team innerhalb des europäischen Amazon-Netzwerks

A day in the life
Deine Betreuung im Programm
Du bist nicht allein. Während des gesamten Programms wirst du von zwei Seiten unterstützt:
• Dein:e Learning Manager:in am Standort begleitet dich durch alle drei Phasen, ist deine zentrale Ansprechperson und koordiniert deine Entwicklung
• Operative Führungskräfte mentoren dich während deiner Rotationen und geben dir direktes Feedback aus der Praxis
Zusätzlich bist du Teil einer deutschlandweiten Community dualer Student:innen - ein Netzwerk, das mit dir wächst.

________________________________________
Dein Alltag: Theorie und Praxis im Wochentakt
Das Studium läuft parallel zur Praxis - keine langen Blockphasen, sondern ein wöchentlicher Rhythmus:
• 2 Tage Studium an deinem IU-Standort (Logistik, Supply Chain, BWL, Personalführung)
• 2-3 Tage / 20 Stunden im Amazon Fulfillment Center oder Sort Center

Du bist kein Besucher im Betrieb. Du bist Teil des Teams - von Tag eins an.

- Allgemeine Hochschulreife, Fachhochschulreife / fachgebundene Hochschulreife
- Fließende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (C1-Niveau)
- Fortgeschrittene Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (B2-Niveau)
- Affinität für das Fach Mathematik
- Umgang mit MS-Office (insbesondere Kenntnisse in Excel, Word und PowerPoint)

title: Sr. PCBA Manufacturing Engineer, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

As a Sr. Aerospace Manufacturing Engineer for one or more Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBA), you'll be directly responsible for bring engineering designs for complex electronic assemblies to reality. You'll work closely with the Design Engineering and Supplier Manufacturing teams to ensure new designs are optimized for manufacturing while driving improvements in yield, cycle time, and cost for existing hardware. Your expertise will be invaluable in bringing satellite hardware to life.

Come solve the difficult and rewarding engineering challenges in developing a highly reliable, power efficient, performant, low-cost satellite bus and payload. As a Sr. PCBA Manufacturing Engineer, you will work across design engineering, supply-chain, quality, and our manufacturing partners to drive Amazon Leo electrical sub-system and PCBA manufacturing and delivery.

You must have the ability to dive deep on the details to identify, understand and solve difficult technical problems and also utilize a system level approach to prioritize issues for whole program. You use data to drive manufacturability, reliability, and quality objectives in design and development teams.

*Up to 25% Travel will be required for this role

Key job responsibilities
-Partner with the Design Engineering teams to drive Design for Excellence (DFx) by providing PCB/PCBA DFM and DFA feedback to identify and mitigate PCBA manufacturing challenges early in product development.

-Own the PCBA Manufacturing Qualification process at the contract manufacturer by defining manufacturing readiness requirements and leading key milestone reviews to ensure all production readiness deliverables are complete.

-Investigate and develop new manufacturing technology and methodologies to enhance PCB and PCBA quality, reliability, throughput, and cost.

-Drive closure of all operational issues during pre-production builds. Work within Operations, Supply Chain, R&D, and Reliability Engineering to implement and optimize manufacturing processes and improve yields for production ramp.

-Investigate failures/defects in manufacturing, test, and integration. Identify and mitigate underlying root causes to prevent reoccurrence as part of continuous improvement efforts.

-Identify opportunities for risk reduction and simplification of PCBA manufacturing processes.

-Deliver manufacturing processes capabilities including equipment capability, quality controls, materials characterization, and standardized rework practices.

-Actively monitor the success of products and processes through production ramp. Provide regular status reports of PCBAs progress from design to production.

-Deploy and qualify polymerics (staking, underfill, and conformal coat) processes for high volume production.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production
- 5+ years of experience in PCBA/PCB manufacturing engineering.
- Experience with driving DFx, DFM, DFA for NPI and mass production
- Experience in board assembly processes: stencil, paste print, SPI, pick & place, SMT reflow, AOI, AXI, selective solder, flying probe, and wash.
- Experience working independently and ensuring timely and accurate communication with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and 3rd party test and failure analysis partners.
- Ability to lead small teams in root-causing technical product manufacturability and process problems and drive implementation of solutions.
- Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, enthusiasm for the team’s spirit of innovation and mission of improving manufacturability, quality, and reliability in cutting-edge technology.

Preferred qualifications

- 7+ years of experience in PCBA/PCB supply chain, manufacturing or engineering.
- 5+ years’ experience with industry standard PLM and DFX systems, Mentor/Valor preferred.
- Experience performing Design and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analyses.
- Experience with IPC-A-610 Class 3, IPC J-STD-001 compliance
- Experience in solder alloys including leaded and lead free as well as next gen low temp alloys.
- Experience leading Design of Experiments.

title: Brand Specialist
descriptionHtml:
About Amazon

Amazon strives to be Earth's most customer-centric company where people can find and discover virtually anything they want to buy online. By giving customers more of what they want - low prices, vast selection, and convenience – Amazon continues to grow and evolve as a world-class e-commerce platform. Amazon's evolution from website to e-commerce partner to development platform is driven by the spirit of innovation that is part of the company's DNA. The world's brightest technology minds come to Amazon to research and develop technology that improves the lives of shoppers and sellers around the world.

About the Role

Account Management- Brand Specialist

As a Brand Specialist you would be a part of Amazon Vendor Services (AVS) Team of Retail Business Services, you will have the exciting opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy for managing Amazon AVS vendors.

AVS team is looking for a bright, customer centric, driven, and creative candidate to join our team. You will interface internally with leaders from our Retail and Vendor Services teams and will be responsible for all aspects of the vendor’s business with Amazon. You will engage directly with multiple internal teams to optimize the product line for key manufacturers (vendors) on Amazon.

You will utilize a wide range of skills and work across major functional areas such as site merchandising, buying, inventory management, finance, operations and online marketing, to drive the performance of strategic vendor partners at Amazon. In this role you will be focused on operational aspects of managing the customer relationships with our vendors.

You will conceive, create and analyze a wide range of marketing activities/campaigns to grow the vendor’s traffic, brand awareness, customer conversion, and revenue on Amazon. Also, you will look into operational aspects of vendor’s business with Amazon, root cause analysis of issues and opportunities affecting business.

Timings will be as per EU shift, 12:00 pm IST to 9:00 pm IST


Key job responsibilities
• Establish long term partnerships with key vendor partners for the group of vendors handled.

• Partnering with the Retail Category Team and build successful communication channels at all levels, set proper expectations, provide clear status communications, and manage towards a growth plan for the vendors.

• Build and execute on a joint business plan that delivers on key business opportunities and relevant KPIs for the vendors and Amazon.

• Conduct deep dive analysis on vendor issues and publish recommendations and action plans based on data to improve vendor experience.

• Success will be measured by the performance of your vendors on input metrics and impact on creating a great customer experience for buying consumers.

• Conduct regular WBRs, MBRs with the vendors, highlight business metric performance and building action plans.

Basic qualifications

- Experience with Excel
- 2+ years of Account Management/Vendor Management

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of Account Management/Vendor Management

Account Management- Brand Specialist (Italian)

As a Brand Specialist as part of Amazon Vendor Services (AVS) Team of Retail Business Services, you will have the exciting opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy for managing Amazon AVS vendors.

AVS team is looking for a bright, customer obsessed, driven, and creative candidate to join our team. You will interface internally with leaders from our Retail and Vendor Services teams and will be responsible for all aspects of the vendor’s business with Amazon. You will engage directly with multiple internal teams to optimize the product line for key manufacturers (vendors) on Amazon.com. You will utilize a wide range of skills and work across major functional areas such as site merchandising, buying, inventory management, finance, operations and online marketing, to drive the performance of strategic vendor partners at Amazon. In this role you will be focused on the strategic and operational aspects of managing the customer relationships with our vendors.

You will conceive, create and analyze a wide range of marketing and site merchandising efforts, to include marketing campaigns to grow the vendor’s traffic, brand awareness, customer conversion, and revenue on Amazon. Also you will look into strategic and operational aspects of their business with Amazon, root cause analysis of issues and opportunities affecting the vendor’s business.

Responsibilities Include

· Success will be measured by the performance of your internal teams on input metrics and impact of vendors on creating a great customer experience for buying consumers

· Partnering with the Retail Category Team and managing the vendor relationship by championing the vendor’s needs at Amazon

· Build strong communication channels at all levels, set proper expectations, provide clear status communications, and manage towards a growth plan for the vendors

· Build and execute on a strategic account plan that delivers on key business opportunities and relevant KPIs for the vendors and Amazon

· Work with internal Amazon teams/vendors to improve operational aspects of their business in providing a great consumer experience

· Conduct deep dive analysis on the handled issues for the vendors and publish recommendations and action plans based on data to improve vendor experience

· Provide thought leadership around planning, roadmaps and execution

· Establish long term partnerships with key vendor partners for the group of vendors handled

· Support the launches of new programs, categories and features

· Conduct regular WBR, MBRs with the vendors highlight business metric performance and building action plans
· Operate in a fast-moving and sometimes ambiguous environment with full control and responsibility of achieving business objectives
· Develop original ideas, approaches, and solutions to typical, unusual or difficult situations or problems
· Demonstrate active listening skills, highly consultative and solutions-oriented

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- MBA, or Master's degree

title: Duales Studium - BWL
descriptionHtml:
Ein Job im Operations-Bereich bei Amazon versetzt dich ins Zentrum dessen, wie Dinge vom Klick bis zur Haustür gelangen. Du hilfst dabei, Systeme zu entwerfen, zu verbessern und zu betreiben, die Menschen, Produkte und Orte miteinander verbinden – und das in großem Maßstab. Du übernimmst früh Verantwortung, arbeitest eng mit Teams zusammen, um reale Herausforderungen zu lösen, und siehst die direkten Ergebnisse deiner Entscheidungen, wenn sie täglich bei den Kunden ankommen. Hier ist die Wirkung dessen, was du aufbaust, nicht abstrakt – sie ist sichtbar, unmittelbar und bedeutsam – und hält eine der komplexesten Betriebsorganisationen der Welt am Laufen. Hier nimmt deine Reise Gestalt an – durch Handeln, Verantwortung und die Möglichkeit, in viele Richtungen zu wachsen Dein Einstieg in die Führung - Das Duale Studium bei Amazon
- Studiengang: BWL / Logistikmanagement (B.A.)
- Studienpartner: IU Internationale Hochschule (30+ Standorte deutschlandweit)
- Programmbeginn: 1. August 2027
- Dauer: 3,5 Jahre
- Einsatzorte: mehr als 20 Amazon-Standorte in Deutschland (Fulfillment Center und Sort Center)
Das duale Studium bei Amazon ist ein strukturiertes Führungsentwicklungsprogramm, das dich Schritt für Schritt auf eine operative Führungsrolle vorbereitet. Wer das Programm erfolgreich abschließt, hat die Chance direkt eine Position als Area Manager:in in unserem Netzwerk zu bekommen - ohne weiteres Bewerbungsverfahren.
________________________________________
Drei Phasen auf dem Weg zur Führungskraft
Das Programm ist in drei aufeinander aufbauende Phasen gegliedert, die deinen Verantwortungsbereich kontinuierlich erweitern.
Phase 1 - Operative Grundlagen: Zunächst lernst du die operativen Abläufe im Fulfillment Center von Grund auf kennen, analysierst Kennzahlen und setzt eigenständig Projekte zur Prozessverbesserung um.
Phase 2 - Rotation & Führungsentwicklung: Anschließend rotierst du durch verschiedene operative Bereiche, übernimmst schrittweise Führungsaufgaben - von der Begleitung der Team Leads über Schichtplanung bis hin zur Personalsteuerung - und entwickelst ein Verständnis für bereichsübergreifende Zusammenhänge.
Phase 3 - Area-Manager-Niveau: In der Abschlussphase arbeitest du auf Area-Manager-Niveau: Du steuerst operative Kennzahlen, führst Teams eigenständig und trägst echte Verantwortung für deinen Bereich.

Das bieten wir dir
• Karriereperspektive: Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Programms wechselst du direkt in eine Area Manager Position im Amazon-Netzwerk - ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren
• Studienfinanzierung: Amazon übernimmt die Studiengebühren an der IU
• Mentoring: Strukturierte Begleitung durch Learning Manager:in und operative Führungskräfte
• Netzwerk: Zugang zu einem europaweiten Operations-Netzwerk
• Mobilität: Kostenloses Deutschlandticket
• Verpflegung: Bezuschusste Mahlzeiten am Standort
• Mitarbeitervorteile: Vielfältige Vorteile, wie ein Amazon Mitarbeiterrabatt
• Technologie: Arbeite täglich mit modernster Automatisierungs- und Robotiktechnologie

Key job responsibilities
• Analyse und Optimierung operativer Prozesse in Fulfillment- und Sortierbereichen
• Eigenständige Durchführung von Continuous Improvement Projekten mit messbaren Ergebnissen
• Übernahme von Führungsaufgaben im Rahmen von Lead-Rotationen (Schichtverantwortung, Teamsteuerung, KPI-Management)
• Mitarbeit an bereichsübergreifenden Projekten in den Bereichen Arbeitssicherheit, Prozessoptimierung, Personalwesen und Technik
• Vorbereitung auf die eigenständige Steuerung eines operativen Bereichs als Area Manager:in
• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit einem internationalen Team innerhalb des europäischen Amazon-Netzwerks

A day in the life
Deine Betreuung im Programm
Du bist nicht allein. Während des gesamten Programms wirst du von zwei Seiten unterstützt:
• Dein:e Learning Manager:in am Standort begleitet dich durch alle drei Phasen, ist deine zentrale Ansprechperson und koordiniert deine Entwicklung
• Operative Führungskräfte mentoren dich während deiner Rotationen und geben dir direktes Feedback aus der Praxis
Zusätzlich bist du Teil einer deutschlandweiten Community dualer Student:innen - ein Netzwerk, das mit dir wächst.

________________________________________
Dein Alltag: Theorie und Praxis im Wochentakt
Das Studium läuft parallel zur Praxis - keine langen Blockphasen, sondern ein wöchentlicher Rhythmus:
• 2 Tage Studium an deinem IU-Standort (Logistik, Supply Chain, BWL, Personalführung)
• 2-3 Tage / 20 Stunden im Amazon Fulfillment Center oder Sort Center

Du bist kein Besucher im Betrieb. Du bist Teil des Teams - von Tag eins an.

Basic qualifications

- Allgemeine Hochschulreife, Fachhochschulreife / fachgebundene Hochschulreife
- Fließende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (C1-Niveau)
- Fortgeschrittene Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (B2-Niveau)
- Affinität für das Fach Mathematik
- Umgang mit MS-Office (insbesondere Kenntnisse in Excel, Word und PowerPoint)

Preferred qualifications

- Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit
- Eigeninitiative, Vorbildfunktion und „Hands-on-Mentalität"
- Interesse, Führungsverantwortung zu tragen

Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. Please consult our Privacy Notice (https://www.amazon.jobs/en/privacy_page) to know more about how we collect, use and transfer the personal data of our candidates.

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

This role will be physically based at our new MDD Pecos, TX site.


Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of electrical facilities maintenance, or 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field

title: Sr. Program Manager, Talent Acquisition Learning
descriptionHtml:
The Global Talent Acquisition (GTA) Learning team is seeking a Sr. Program Manager, Knowledge Management to own the establishment of a knowledge management system in PXT's Create Once, Reuse Everywhere (COREx) system, supporting an initiative to certify 100% of GTA standard work content in COREx for AI assistant consumption. This role is the operational engine of that mission: driving migration execution, enforcing content governance, and managing the end-to-end content lifecycle so that Talent Acquisition and AI tools draw from a single, certified source of truth. The Sr. Program Manager reports directly to the Sr. Manager of TA Learning.


You will own the strategy and operational execution that turns fragmented, legacy knowledge into governed, discoverable, certified content: batching and migrating content from a variety of source material, running the intake mechanism for ad hoc certification requests, maintaining the Playbook and SOPs, and driving down the content backlog. You operate independently, bring order to ambiguity, and hold partner teams accountable to governance standards without direct authority. This role partners closely with the COREx Integration Lead, who owns Aza integration, retrieval accuracy, and TA Hub evolution. Where that role ensures certified content surfaces accurately in AI-powered tools, this role ensures the content is migrated, governed, and certified in the first place — together forming the two halves of the COREx content operating model.

Key job responsibilities
Content Migration & Execution: Own end-to-end content migration—batching pages by parent process or topic, running them through AI quality scoring, and driving owner review to migration or deprecation. Keep prep for the next batch running concurrently with current reviews to protect timelines. Drive down the content backlog using phased prioritization by content pillar.

Governance & Content Lifecycle: Maintain the COREx Migration Playbook and SOPs for Talent Acquisition, keeping submission, certification, and publication standards current as the program scales. Enforce the governance framework across Recruiting Operations Center (ROC) teams, tying certification to disposition criteria (Migrate, Consolidate, Retire, Defer). Own the post-migration lifecycle, running maintenance cycles that validate the governance model and flag content needing updates.

Intake & Coordination: Run central intake for ad hoc certification requests—triaging against criteria, leading a ROC tiger team to identify owners and next steps, and defining response SLAs. Design change management campaigns that drive adoption of COREx standards, measuring adoption and self-service use. Establish the partner-team checkpoint tying Mercury publishing to COREx upload confirmation.

Quality Assurance & Certification: Operate the QA framework governing quality scoring against COREx standards. Leverage AI-assisted review to scale checks across accuracy, completeness, voice, terminology, and accessibility. Ensure migrated content is certified, accessible, discoverable, and clearly owned, with deprecation/redirect paths in place.

Metrics & Reporting: Define, track, and report core metrics alongside migration completion data. Report to three audiences: the migration team (operational), ROC leadership (status), and ROC stakeholders (goal attainment).

A day in the life
You operate the system that moves GTA's knowledge base from fragmented tribal content into a governed, certified single source of truth on COREx — owning the pipeline end-to-end and holding the org accountable to quality and timeline.


On a typical day, you run batch triage on incoming certification requests, dispositioning each against governance criteria and routing owners into the pipeline. You monitor active migration batches — nudging content owners through their 30-day review window, clearing permissions blockers, and escalating unresponsive owners per the defined path. You review AI-generated quality scores, refine change recommendations, and maintain the Asana board that tracks status across the portfolio.


You partner outward as much as inward: working with ROC PMs to drive self-service adoption, unblock complex content sets, and reinforce upload SLAs; aligning with the COREx Integration Lead to ensure certified content surfaces accurately in Aza and the TA Hub; and keeping the Playbook and SOPs current as the operating model evolves — all in service of a governed, certified, single source of truth for GTA knowledge.

About the team
TA Learning sits within the Recruiting Operations Center (ROC) and owns the enablement and knowledge management for Global Talent Acquisition. The team leads the COREx migration — consolidating fragmented recruiting knowledge scattered across Wiki, Sage, Broadcast, AtoZ, and other platforms into a single certified source of truth that both recruiters and AI assistants can trust. The team is also responsible for onboarding, skills development, interviewer readiness, and product education.


This role is one of two that operationalizes the TA knowledge management system. You own the knowledge management engine: Migration, governance, lifecycle, and intake. While your partner owns Aza integration: Retrieval accuracy, and the evolution of the TA Hub into a multi-audience, AI-enabled enablement platform. Together, the two roles ensure content is both certified at the source and surfaced accurately at the point of need.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience with content or knowledge management systems, content lifecycle management, and governance frameworks.

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience leading organizational change initiatives across multiple locations
- Experience defining and enforcing taxonomy, information architecture, or content certification standards at scale.
- Experience establishing intake mechanisms, SLAs, and operational cadences (batch triage, maintenance cycles) for a content or process program.
- Experience working with AI-powered content tooling (quality assessment, retrieval, or AI assistants) and understanding how certified content feeds AI systems.

descriptionHtml:

To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Amazon has built a reputation for excellence with recent examples of being named #1 in customer service, #1 most trusted, and #2 most innovative. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is carrying on that tradition while leading the world in Cloud technologies. AWS Support provides global technical support to a wide range of external customers as they build mission-critical applications on top of AWS services. As a member of the AWS Support team you will be at the forefront of this transformational technology - assisting a global list of companies that are taking advantage of a growing set of services and features to run their mission-critical applications.

We are looking for a technical leader who will lead teams in our Customer Interaction Management organization (CIM). CIM owns the products that ensure AWS customers can always get support and the frontline builders who provide support to our customers. Our services need to be highly scalable, highly available, handle diverse frameworks and integrations, and make it easier for our customers to interact with our Support organization. The technical leader needs to be able to evaluate and evolve our technology stack as the cloud around them evolves in an era of GenAI and be ready to invent new ways of solving exciting new challenges every day. The leader should be a strong operator who is comfortable operating production systems that hundreds of thousands of Enterprise and Business customers depend on.

You are passionate about improving AWS customers' support experience and executing on our vision of integrated support building innovative support products using the latest GenAI technologies to create delightful customer experiences while allowing our support organization to scale. You will be responsible for leading a team of engineers and responsible for their career growth and job satisfaction.

• Product You will closely partner with your product manager to define and execute on the vision for your product. You will set and help your development team maintain line-of-sight to key product goals.
• Projects You will be responsible for developing a roadmap and delivery plan for your team as well as track progress against key goals. You will identify dependencies and risks and mitigate risks before they start to impact project goals and manage expectations when things don't go as planned.
• Process You, together with your team, own the team's development process. You should be comfortable running an agile development process and ensure it serves the team rather than the team serving it.
• People You will own all facets of performance management and career development for your team. Helping team members achieve their career objectives through regular one-on-one engagements is required. You will mentor all members in order to maintain a well-rounded world class organization. title: Senior Manager, EC2 Nitro, EC2 Nitro
descriptionHtml:
EC2 Nitro drives the planet's largest, fastest growing, and most feature-rich compute cloud, and EC2 Machine Learning Systems (MLS) is where that platform meets the most demanding AI workloads on Earth. We build and scale the compute platforms behind AWS's largest ML training and inference clusters — integrating custom hardware, firmware, systems software, and services to turn AI accelerators (NVIDIA GB200/GB300/VeraRubin-class UltraServer/UltraCluster) into reliable, high-performance capacity for customers ranging from startups to the largest AI labs in the world.

We are looking for a seasoned engineering leader to own an existing, at-scale ML compute platform and to set and drive its multi-year technical strategy. As a Senior Manager leading a team of 3–5 managers and roughly 40–50 engineers, you will be responsible for the health, velocity, and long-term direction of an organization that spans hardware bring-up, firmware, cluster management, and application software. You will define where the platform needs to be several years out, make the architectural and investment bets that get us there, and build the org — leaders, senior engineers, and mechanisms — capable of delivering it.

In this role, you will operate at the intersection of a broad and deep set of technical teams. You will partner at a senior level with silicon and hardware partners (Annapurna and NVIDIA) to co-design and bring up NVIDIA GB200/GB300 platforms and UltraServer/UltraCluster systems, and with science, ML framework, and other AWS service organizations to remove ambiguity, align roadmaps, and land capabilities that no single team could deliver alone. You will be measured not only on what your organization ships, but on the clarity of the technical strategy you set and your ability to influence direction well beyond your immediate teams.

The ideal candidate:

- Has a deep technical background in systems software — sufficient to earn the trust of senior engineers and make sound architectural and design judgments in a Linux environment involving C, C++, and/or Rust. You will not be writing production code day-to-day, but you must be able to go deep, ask the right questions, and hold a high technical bar.
- Brings strong operational instincts for large-scale software delivery — version control, automated build and release, and software quality practices — and knows how to instill them across an organization.
- Has in-depth knowledge of ML frameworks and cluster management, and understands the workloads and failure modes of large-scale ML training and inference at cluster scale.
- Has a track record of setting multi-year technical strategy, driving org-level execution through other managers, and influencing partners across organizational boundaries.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of engineering experience
- 5+ years of engineering team management experience
- 10+ years of planning, designing, developing and delivering consumer software experience
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams
- Experience managing multiple concurrent programs, projects and development teams in an Agile environment

Preferred qualifications

- Experience partnering with product and program management teams
- Experience participating in or leading technical collaborations and creating alignment across diverse groups (e.g., hardware engineering, software engineering, program management)
- Experience hiring, developing and promoting engineering talent

descriptionHtml:

You will own the commercial strategy and customer relationships across the company's Upstream and Downstream operations, driving the next wave of cloud and AI adoption in one of the most transformational accounts in the energy sector.

You will define and execute a CXO-level relationship strategy with the customer's operational leadership, coordinate alignment with main Industry Vertical Vendors, and shape the customer's digital transformation roadmap. descriptionHtml:
Technical Operations & Partner Services (TOPS) supports 549 Whole Foods Market stores through 12+ technology vendor partners, managing thousands of service operations monthly. Much of this work is still manual — and that's where you come in.

As Program Manager for Automation & Vendor Operations, you'll own the strategy and delivery of automation solutions that eliminate manual touchpoints across vendor management and service delivery. Starting with ServiceNow workflow optimization, you'll design automated ticket routing, SLA monitoring, escalation triggers, and reporting pipelines — then expand into AI-enabled operations like anomaly detection and predictive escalation. You'll partner closely with Service Delivery and Vendor Programs to free Program Managers from operational mechanics so they can focus on strategic vendor accountability.

This is a build-from-scratch opportunity with high visibility to leadership and a direct line to vendor operations impact across the network.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the TOPS Automation Roadmap — maintain a prioritized backlog of automation opportunities ranked by effort vs. impact, and deliver against it
- Map current-state ServiceNow workflows (ticket routing, SLA management, escalation paths, vendor dispatch) and design automated replacements
- Build automated SLA monitoring and escalation triggers that alert Program Managers to at-risk tickets before breach
- Develop automated reporting pipelines that pull ServiceNow data into standardized weekly/monthly outputs without manual intervention
- Extend AI-assisted analysis into vendor management workflows — anomaly detection, predictive escalation, and ticket pattern analysis
- Explore and pilot generative AI applications for vendor communications, QBR preparation, and performance narrative generation
- Define success metrics for each automation initiative (hours saved, error reduction, speed improvement) and track delivery against targets
- Document manual processes with sufficient detail to enable automation design — process maps, decision trees, exception handling
- Build solutions that are maintainable by the TOPS team, not dependent on specialized engineering support
- Coordinate with Vendor Performance Analyst to ensure automated data collection feeds the analytics layer accurately
- Communicate automation progress and ROI to leadership through monthly updates and quarterly business reviews

A day in the life
Your morning starts reviewing the automated overnight SLA monitoring report — three vendors flagged for resolution time drift. The system sent vendor notifications and escalated to the assigned PM. You check the automation dashboard for support process audit confidence and by Mid-morning, you're in a working session with the ServiceNow platform team, configuring a new Flow Designer workflow that will auto-generate weekly vendor compliance summaries — eliminating 4 hours of manual PM work per week. After lunch, you partner with the Vendor Performance Analyst to validate that your automated data feeds are populating the scorecard accurately. You close the day updating the automation roadmap: the QBR auto-preparation pilot showed promising results, and you're drafting the business case to scale it across all 7 vendor programs. Every automation you ship gives a PM back hours they can invest in holding vendors accountable rather than chasing data.

About the team
TOPS is the team that keeps technology running across 549 Whole Foods Market stores — managing 12+ vendor partners and driving accountability through data, not assumptions. Our core tenets say it best: we deep dive with data until it reveals clear insights, we're steamrollers with smiles, and we win as one team. This is a builder's environment — we're actively transforming reactive vendor management into a proactive, predictive operation. If you want ownership from Day 1, high visibility to leadership, and a team that has a little fun while delivering results, you'll fit right in.

- 3+ years of program or project management experience

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

descriptionHtml:

ABOUT AMAZON

Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Rapid and Rural Logistics (R2L) is an exciting organization within Amazon specializing in delighting our customers with speed in which we can make items appear on their doorsteps. Rural Super Rural (RSR) is a subset of R2L dedicated to ensuring our customers receive their deliveries and are satisfied with their service, even in our most remote area. descriptionHtml:
The Controls Integration Engineer supports the on-site deployment, integration, and commissioning of automated material handling equipment such as sorters, conveyor systems, and automated work cells. This role is hands-on and execution-focused, working alongside senior engineers to bring up Industrial PCs (IPCs), PLCs, industrial networks, and field devices during installation and commissioning phases.

This is an early-career technical role designed for engineers with strong foundational knowledge in controls, electrical systems, and industrial automation who are ready to develop field commissioning expertise. The engineer will receive mentorship and technical direction from Sr Controls Integration Engineers while progressively taking on greater ownership of commissioning tasks and subsystems.


Key job responsibilities
Deployment & Commissioning Support
• Support on-site commissioning activities for sorters, conveyors, and automated work cells under the direction of senior engineers.
• Assist with provisioning, configuring, and validating Linux-based IPCs, PLCs, HMIs, industrial networks, and field devices per project standards.
• Perform I/O checkouts, point-to-point wiring verification, and device-level validation.
• Execute defined commissioning and test procedures, documenting results and flagging deviations.
• Support dry runs, functional testing, and integrated system testing during startup phases.
Troubleshooting & Technical Support
• Troubleshoot device-level and subsystem-level issues including sensor faults, communication errors, wiring discrepancies, and basic PLC logic issues.
• Escalate complex or multi-domain issues to senior engineers with clear documentation of symptoms, steps taken, and observations.
• Assist with industrial network validation including IP addressing, device discovery, and basic switch configuration verification.
• Document issues, resolutions, and lessons learned to support team knowledge sharing.
On-Site Execution & Coordination
• Work alongside technicians, electricians, and contractors during system installation and commissioning.
• Follow safety requirements, quality standards, and commissioning procedures at all times.
• Communicate status, blockers, and progress to the on-site lead engineer clearly and proactively.
• Maintain organized records of commissioning progress, punch lists, and test results.
Integration & Handover Support

descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. The Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) team sets the strategic direction to provide resources, best practices, and safe environments to proactively manage the health and wellbeing of our workforce. The OMR will function as a part of the larger team onsite, assisting with all first aid needs and support safety operations as needed.

Minimize the AA risk of injury through awareness, education, and proactive engagement.
Maintain all records of care provided to AAs.
Coordinate and maintain the workers’ compensation and return to work programs for AAs with work-related injuries.
Provide daily activity logs and end of shift reports.
Engage with AAs and leadership on operations floor to provide coaching regarding observed at-risk work habits.
Maintain a clean working environment and ensure appropriate medical supply inventory is maintained.
Participate in training and certification to facilitate first aid, CPR and AED certifications classes.
Maintain all first aid, CPR, AED credentials.
Work flexible shifts which could include days, nights, holidays, and/or weekends.
Assist with random saliva drug testing protocols.
Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site.


Additional Job Elements include:

Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
Work in an environment where the noise level varies
Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)


For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

title: NA Food Safety Audit & Monitoring Manager, NA Food Safety Audit & Monitoring
descriptionHtml:
Job Description
The North American Food Safety Audit & Monitoring (A&M) Team ensures Amazon sites meet food safety standards, regulatory requirements, and internal compliance expectations through independent audit and monitoring activities. The team partners with a broad range of internal stakeholders to identify compliance risks, provide data-driven insights, and deliver recommendations that support continuous improvement across the fulfillment network.

The Food Safety A&M Manager is responsible for translating audit and monitoring outputs into clear risk insights and actionable recommendations for partner teams, while maintaining independence in assessment, verification, and enforcement activities. This role collaborates closely with Operations, Food Safety Programs, Risk, and other cross-functional stakeholders to support scalable compliance mechanisms and improve food safety performance across the network.

The successful candidate demonstrates strong analytical capabilities, sound operational judgment, and the ability to influence stakeholders through data, trend analysis, and risk-based recommendations. They are able to identify systemic risks, communicate findings effectively to leadership, and ensure compliance concerns are appropriately escalated and tracked through resolution by the responsible partner teams.

We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations: Arlington, VA, USA and Bellevue, WA, USA

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities

• Execute independent audit and monitoring activities to assess compliance with food safety standards, regulatory requirements, and internal policies across the fulfillment network

• Maintain and analyze compliance metrics, audit outputs, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement

• Assess and escalate significant food safety risks identified through audits, monitoring activities, customer complaints, and trend analysis, ensuring appropriate visibility to partner teams and senior leadership

• Influence and partner effectively with cross-functional stakeholders, including Operations, Food Safety Programs, Risk, and support teams, to communicate findings, provide risk-based recommendations, and drive alignment on remediation expectations

• Analyze audit findings, customer complaints, escalation data, and root cause trends to identify systemic risks and inform audit strategies, monitoring priorities, and leadership reporting

• Develop and present business review narratives, audit insights, and leadership updates that clearly communicate compliance risks, operational trends, and recommended actions

• Apply knowledge of regulatory frameworks, including the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA), and FDA guidance, to support audit consistency, monitoring mechanisms, and compliance assessments

• Review and assess audit observations, and compliance-related data to ensure appropriate documentation, escalation and identification of recurring risk patterns

We are seeking experienced CHDEs to architect, design, develop, and build next-generation server and rack solutions. Our designs are industry-leading in performance, frugality and operational excellence, and are critical to the success of the AWS business and the more than one million customers who use AWS today. title: Sr. Applied Scientist, Alexa Smart Home
descriptionHtml:
Alexa Smart Home Science builds the intelligence that lets customers control and automate their homes naturally, spanning voice understanding, proactive automation, habit and preference learning, and the LLM/agentic systems that power the next generation of ambient home experiences. We are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to own the scientific direction of a major workstream, turning ambiguous, open-ended problems into production systems that measurably improve the customer experience across millions of homes.
You will define the research agenda for your area, partner deeply with engineering to bring models into production, and raise the scientific bar
across the broader team. You will work at the intersection of large language models, agentic orchestration, personalization, and real-world heterogeneity across homes, devices, and occupants. This is a hands-on role: you will frame the problems, build the models, guide the system design, and mentor other scientists, while influencing product and technical roadmaps beyond your immediate team.

Key job responsibilities
- Independently identify, frame, and solve ill-defined research problems tied to broad Smart Home problem areas, delivering with limited guidance.
- Define system-level technical requirements and partner with engineering teams to adapt scientific techniques to meet production constraints (latency, cost, reliability), making appropriate tradeoffs.
- Own the science strategy and roadmap for a workstream; anticipate future business and technical requirements.
- Design and run rigorous experimentation and evaluation to validate approaches and quantify customer/business impact.
- Build consensus on scientific approach and best practices across multiple teams; influence product features and technical direction beyond your own team.
- Actively mentor and develop other scientists, and raise the bar in hiring.
- Contribute to the internal and external scientific community through publications, patents, and dissemination of scientific artifacts.

A day in the life
No two days look alike, but the throughline is owning a scientific problem from question to production impact. You might dig into evaluation results to find where the experience falls short, frame a hypothesis, and prototype with LLMs or agentic techniques. You will pair with engineering to turn a promising model into a production-ready design, weighing latency, cost, and reliability tradeoffs. Expect alignment with product managers on customer problems, working sessions with fellow scientists, and time mentoring teammates. Your customers are Alexa smart home users across millions of households; your stakeholders span product, engineering, and partner science teams.

About the team
We are the science team behind Alexa's smart home experience. We are applied scientists and science engineers making the home genuinely intelligent: anticipatory, personalized, and effortless. Our mission is to move Alexa from reacting to commands toward understanding a household's rhythms and acting helpfully on the customer's behalf, reliably and at scale. Because no two homes are alike, we embrace that diversity rather than paper over it. We value research-grounded decisions, hands-on work, and long-horizon bets. Scientists own their areas end-to-end, mentor one another, publish, and partner closely with engineering and product.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience
- PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience with neural deep learning methods and machine learning

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
- Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

title: Data Center Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

- Technical writing to support change management program

- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

- This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

- Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 4+ years of military experience

descriptionHtml:

Your initiatives will shape strategy, drive customer satisfaction, and drive business growth and profitability across one of Amazon's most critical areas.

The role focuses on identifying opportunities and gaps in concessions & returns policies, operating procedures, network and product/program's logic, while designing, developing and executing a comprehensive master plan with strategic initiatives to improve the way we serve our customers.

title: Senior Accelerator Engineer, Cloud AI/ML server team
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 5, 2026

Do you want to become the go-to GPU expert for the world's largest Artificial Intelligence accelerator fleet, and grow that expertise faster than anywhere else in the industry?

This is a role where you will deepen your GPU expertise at a pace and scale that doesn't exist outside of hyperscale cloud, working directly with the industry's leading GPU vendors, analyzing behaviors across hundreds of thousands of accelerators, and defining standards that govern production deployment. If you have started to develop GPU or accelerator depth and want a position where you own the full lifecycle at fleet scale, this is the role!

AWS Hardware Engineering is looking for a Senior Hardware Development Engineer to own the technical roadmap across all AI accelerator platforms in the organization. You will be the single-threaded owner of GPU lifecycle from defining hardware, firmware and diagnostics requirements, qualification through field operations and translating fleet-scale failure data into vendor action.


Key job responsibilities
GPU Component Lifecycle & Strategy

- Own the technical relationship with vendors across all platforms in the portfolio: roadmap alignment, escalations, partnerships.
- Own qualification of new GPU SKUs and baseboard assemblies during NPI bring-up -- define test plans, acceptance criteria, and production readiness gates
- Define and maintain GPU firmware qualification criteria across the org -- pass/fail gates, staged rollout policy, regression detection methodology
- Drive RMA strategy: build failure evidence packages, negotiate acceptance criteria with vendors, manage submission quotas and pipeline velocity

Fleet-Scale Failure Analysis

- Lead root-cause analysis on fleet-wide GPU failure modes (component errors, PCIE interface errors, thermal events, link degradation, manufacturing escapes) using telemetry, event log data, and vendor diagnostics
- Set GPU health standards: define the metrics, thresholds, and alerting that platform teams execute against
- Define GPU fleet health dashboards: identify relevant telemetry, failure rate trends, replacement pipeline status, firmware version distribution, qualification status

Vendor Engagement & Cross-Team Leadership

- Represent the organization in technical discussions with leading vendor’s engineering -- translate fleet-scale patterns into prioritized vendor action items
- Partner with server teams to ensure consistent GPU operational practices; provide expertise without owning their execution
- Present GPU fleet health, replacement pipeline status, and qualification progress to senior leadership (VP-level) regularly
- Mentor engineers on GPU failure analysis methodology




A day in the life
No two weeks look the same. You might be engaging with our GPU vendor's engineering team on future roadmap options and how upcoming architecture changes affect our technical strategy. You might be defining technical requirements to enable AWS to optimize how we deploy and manage GPUs at scale -- translating fleet failure patterns into firmware feature requests. You might be analyzing thermal and error behaviors across tens of thousands of systems to develop predictive models that catch failures before they impact customers. Or you might be building the data package that proves a manufacturing defect to a vendor and recovers millions in component value.

What's consistent: you are the GPU component owner. You see every failure mode, every firmware release, every new SKU qualification. You develop expertise at a rate that isn't possible when you only see one system at a time -- here you see hundreds of thousands, and you use that scale to become the person both AWS and our vendors turn to for answers.

Located in Cupertino, Seattle, or Denver, you work with global hardware teams, vendor engineering, and cross-AWS accelerator initiatives.


About the team
AWS Hardware Engineering designs and delivers next-generation cloud infrastructure -- the servers, accelerators, and storage platforms that power AWS. Our team builds and operates custom AI accelerator systems at global scale, spanning GPU platforms from manufacturing through multi-year fleet operations. We are directly responsible for the most expensive and supply-constrained components in the AWS fleet.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent
- Experience in developing functional specifications, design verification plans and functional test procedures
- 7+ years of hardware design and development experience for server, compute, or large-scale infrastructure platforms

Preferred qualifications

- 7+ years hardware engineering experience
- Direct experience with data center GPUs and associated tooling
- Experience developing or influencing server roadmap
- Track record of influencing vendor engineering priorities through failure evidence
- Familiarity with GPU thermal management, power delivery, and PCIe and interconnect architectures
- Experience with firmware lifecycle management at scale (qualification, staged rollout, regression detection, rollback)
- Comfortable presenting to VP-level audiences
- Experience working horizontally across multiple platform teams without direct authority
- Strong data analysis skills at fleet scale (statistical failure modeling, trend detection, threshold setting)
