title: Mechanical Integration Leader, OMHS
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis

Amazon is seeking a Mechanical Integration Lead to drive the successful installation, integration, and deployment of material handling equipment (MHE) across multiple greenfield and brownfield fulfillment center sites. This role provides hands-on mechanical engineering leadership in complex automation environments, ensuring projects meet Amazon's safety, timeline, cost, and quality standards. The Mechanical Integration Lead will directly manage mechanical installation crews deploying conveyor systems, sortation equipment, and associated structural systems across North America. Reporting to the Site Deployment Manager, you will lead sub-teams responsible for structural steel installation, conveyor prep and placement, mechanical connections and belting, side guide and netting installation, pneumatic systems, and mechanical quality control and commissioning. You will collaborate across engineering, supply chain, and operations to implement scalable solutions, resolve technical issues in the field, and deliver high-impact results across large, multi-site programs.

Key job responsibilities
Mechanical Installation Leadership:
• Directly manage and lead mechanical installation crews deploying MHE across North American facilities
• Oversee structural header steel installation including hanging steel, prebuilding supports, and anchoring to building structure
• Lead conveyor prep and placement operations — rigging, lifting, staging, and setting conveyor sections into final positions on installed supports
• Manage conveyor connections and belting crews — ensuring proper mechanical alignment, bed connections, squaring, leveling, and hardware tightening
• Direct side guide and netting installation ensuring proper alignment and tension
• Oversee belt crew operations including belting and lacing installation on aligned conveyor sections
• Manage pneumatic/air systems installation including air connections to conveyor components, pressure testing, and leak verification
• Coordinate with the logistics and receiving team to ensure materials are inventoried, staged, and distributed to work zones on schedule

Quality Control & Commissioning:
• Lead mechanical QC and commissioning activities including alignment verification, hardware inspections, and match-mark verification
• Oversee conveyor run-in testing, belt tracking verification, and belt tension checks
• Manage mechanical punch list identification and repair
• Verify IOQ checks and ensure all mechanical systems meet specifications before handoff to electrical teams
• Ensure proper match-marking of nuts/bolts to verify tightness across all connections

Technical Leadership & Standards:
• Provide mechanical engineering expertise for automation initiatives across assigned sites
• Implement technical solutions and lead project-level decisions within the mechanical scope
• Follow and help develop mechanical installation standards and best practices
• Create and maintain technical documentation including work instructions, installation SOPs, and QC checklists
• Participate in design reviews and drive mechanical engineering excellence
• Recommend and implement process improvements to increase installation efficiency and quality

Project Execution & Coordination:
• Lead delivery of complex mechanical installation projects with multi-site impact
• Work cross-functionally with engineering, supply chain, and operations teams
• Coordinate with the electrical integration lead to ensure proper sequencing — mechanical work must be complete in each zone before electrical teams
mobilize
• Manage relationships with mechanical vendors and partners
• Provide technical input to leadership for data-driven decision-making
• Drive achievement of safety, timeline, cost, and quality metrics across assigned zones
• Participate in daily business reviews with installation progress updates

A day in the life
As a Mechanical Integration Lead, you start your day with the site coordination meeting, reviewing progress against the installation schedule and identifying any material or sequencing issues with your crews. From there, you're on the construction
floor — walking zones with your structural steel team verifying header hanger loads, checking that the conveyor prep and placement crew has the right sections staged, and ensuring the connections team is properly aligning and torquing hardware. You troubleshoot rigging challenges, coordinate with the Site Operations Leader on material deliveries, and validate that mechanical QC checks are passed before handing zones off to the electrical team. You close out by updating job plans, flagging risks for the daily business review, and planning tomorrow's crew assignments, ratios, and confirming proper routing around obstructions. You oversee wire pulling operations in active zones, ensuring proper cable sizing, bend radius compliance, and pull tension limits are respected. Mid-morning you inspect control panel placements, verifying mounting locations match drawings, checking clearance requirements, and confirming grounding connections. You validate junction box and disconnect installations, review wire terminations for proper torque values and labeling, and address any field conflicts that require engineering clarification. By afternoon, you're tracking installation progress against the schedule, coordinating with the device installation lead on upcoming zone handoffs, and documenting redlines for as-built updates. You close out at the daily business review with progress updates and flag any material or access risks for the next day.

About the team
The OMHS Installation & Deployment team supports the deployment and integration of automation and material handling systems across Amazon's operations network. The team works cross-functionally with engineering, construction, operations, supply chain, vendors, and field execution partners to deliver safe, scalable, and reliable systems.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in engineering including a supervisory role managing people
- Experience in a fast-paced, automated, industrial, logistics, production or manufacturing environment
- 5+ years of experience in industrial engineering, operations engineering, manufacturing engineering, or project engineering in a manufacturing or construction environment
- Experience in a supervisory role managing installation crews, maintenance technicians, or tradespeople
- Experience with the project management of technical projects in fast-paced, automated industrial environments
- Experience delivering technical projects in active construction environments
- Ability to travel up to 50% domestically; travel may exceed 50% in some instances with short notice. When not traveling you will be on-site at your assigned building.
- Ability to read and understand installation drawings

Preferred qualifications

- Prior experience managing millwrights, maintenance technicians, fabricators, ironworkers, riggers, pipefitters, or aircraft mechanics
- Prior experience working for a material handling integrator
- Prior experience installing conveyor or sortation systems
- Experience with rigging, crane operations, and heavy equipment placement
- Experience with structural steel installation and load verification
- Knowledge of AutoCAD, BIM 360, or equivalent CAD software
- Experience working with and managing third-party vendors and subcontractors
- Experience with Six Sigma, lean manufacturing, or continuous improvement methodologies
- Experience with pneumatic systems installation and testing

title: SSD Mfg NPI Product Engineer, Nitro SSD
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services’ Hardware Engineering team is looking for experienced professionals to help build the world’s premier cloud computing platform. We are looking for Manufacturing Engineers who are capable of operating in a fast paced, ever changing, multi-platform international manufacturing and production environment. Our Manufacturing Engineers work closely with our ODMs, CMs, internal AWS hardware and software development teams, and with upstream component vendors to monitor and improve the incoming hardware quality of AWS products both proactively in the design phase as well as monitoring, reporting and investigating any early-life product failures. This role requires the engineer to be a technical contact and take on full ownership of the manufacturing launch and resolution of process issues. You will be the driver in getting production up and running, understanding root cause of hardware failures and resolving gaps in our suppliers manufacturing processes.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The AWS Hardware Engineering team is driving rapid innovation in the server and storage infrastructure used by Amazon Web Services. Our designs are industry-leading in frugality and operational excellence, and are critical to the success of the AWS business and the more than one million customers who use AWS today.

The ideal candidate for this role will be an innovative self-starter. You will be an hardware manufacturing and reliability expert with experience in large scale production bring up, improving manufacturing quality, reliability and NPI lead time through hardware, software and process optimization. You will work with engineers across the company as well as external companies such as NAND vendor, contract and original design manufacturer on custom solid-state devices. You will collaborate with internal and external development engineers (architecture, hardware, validation, software services). AWS Engineers are shaping the way people use computers and designing the future of cloud computing technology – come help us make history!

What you will do: You will be a member of a team designing AWS-specific hardware, firmware and software for non-volatile memory devices, including NAND-based SSDs. You will be a part of the hardware development and production bring up effort from conception, through validation and into production. You will contribute to hardware development and lead manufacturing workflow optimization and yield/reliability improvement. You will work closely with AWS hardware and software engineers to tailor manufacturing process for the AWS environment.

Why it matters: Public cloud IT services represent the majority of growth in the overall IT services market and will continue to do so for several years to come. The scale of AWS, combined with an understanding of how our hardware is used, creates a unique opportunity for component customizations that will directly benefit our customers.

Why you will love it: You will work with engineers across the company to enable next-generation devices from prototyping to mass production. You will have a direct impact on our bottom line and the ability to deliver improvements for our developers. You will be part of a growing, fast paced, and fun team. You will have ownership for the implementation of your work. You will see direct product improvements based on the results of your work.

Key job responsibilities
- Evaluate and optimize product designs for quality assurance and manufacturing efficiency of solid state drive products and their integration with servers and rack systems
- Scale up manufacturing on new SSD products across a global network.
- Lead and oversee quality control processes across Contract Manufacturers (CM), Original Design Manufacturers (ODM), and component vendors
- Deliver hands-on technical support during new product introductions and launches
- Investigate and resolve customer escalations through comprehensive root cause analysis
- Define hardware reliability qualification plans and drive root cause and customer impact analysis for manufacturing reliability excursions, including AFR and DPPM estimation.
- Drive Operational Readiness Review (ORR) and Ok2Ship for Manufacturing site readiness assessment.

A day in the life
- Participate in production standups and yield review meetings with CM and ODM
- Monitor manufacturing quality metrics and triage hardware or firmware issues in production
- Monitor and audit reliability demonstration tests, reviewing results and driving pass/fail decisions
- Lead cross-functional discussions with NAND vendors, CM, and ODM on process improvements
- Review and interpret reliability test data, driving qualification decisions for new hardware
- Coordinate manufacture-related firmware releases and validate deployment readiness
- Audit manufacturing processes and identify opportunities to improve yield and reduce cycle time
- Report production status, reliability milestones, and risk assessments for Leadership review
- 1:1's with leadership team, hardware/firmware engineers, and key vendor partners


About the team
Nitro SSD is the fastest growing NAND flash-memory based storage solution for AWS. The 3rd generation Nitro SSD is now available for AWS customers on both Intel and Graviton storage platforms. This is the latest milestone in the AWS Nitro SSD strategy. We deliver industry leading performance and tail latency, while offering a cost competitive, high density storage solution for AWS customers. We own ALL the firmware, hardware, software and telemetry/monitoring for ALL the devices in the fleet. We partner will global NAND vendors, SoC vendors and manufacturing partners to drive the full product-lifecycle for Nitro SSD.

AWS Hardware Engineering Services organization support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing Engineering or similar related field or equivalent experience.
- 3+ years of Manufacturing Engineering work experience with storage drives, server platforms or on high-tech hardware
- 2+ years of product development experience
- 2+ years of statistical analysis and reliability testing (JEDEC standards, accelerated life testing)
- Experience with failure analysis techniques to evaluate production and field failures, driving root cause analysis and resolution

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production
- Experience with the project management of technical projects
- Experience with Six Sigma tools and Lean techniques
- Six Sigma Black Belt Certification, or Six Sigma Green Belt
- Experience working with device technologies under development, familiarity with flashing firmware, basic device debugging and familiarity with reading/pulling device logs

title: Sr. Network Support Specialist - Italian & English, eero
descriptionHtml:
**This role would require you to speak, read and write in English & Italian at a minimum of B2 level**
**This role is 5days a week but would require you to work on either of Saturday or Sunday on rotational basis**

At eero, we're on a mission to make connectivity just work. No dead zones, no buffering, no stress. We build the hardware, craft the software, and tie it all together in the cloud to deliver fast, reliable, and secure WiFi for homes and businesses. And we're just getting started. Think smart homes, small business solutions, and the future of connected living.
We're looking for a Sr. Network Support Specialist (Bilingual Italian &English) to join our London team. If you're someone who loves solving tricky tech problems, thrives on helping people, and can switch effortlessly between English and Italian, this could be your next move. You'll be supporting both English speaking and Italian speaking customers across the EMEA region and beyond, so being comfortable communicating in both languages is essential. If you've got some networking knowledge and a feel for WiFi and telecommunications, even better. We'll invest in your growth with hands-on training covering WiFi fundamentals, networking concepts, and all the eero specific tools you'll need to succeed.
You'll be based in our London office, working alongside a brilliant, supportive team in a global company where your career can genuinely grow.


Key job responsibilities
Here's what you'll actually be doing day-to-day:
● Providing advanced technical support to both English-speaking and Italian-speaking customers, as well as Tier 1 colleagues, via phone, email, or chat.
● Getting hands on with network devices, configuring routers, switches, firewalls, and wireless access points.
● Troubleshooting complex network issues like routing, switching, and firewall problems, plus the devices connecting to them.
● Documenting every support interaction so the team can learn and improve together.
● Spotting complex issues and escalating them to higher tier support teams when needed.
● Mentoring and coaching junior team members, sharing what you know and helping them level up.
● Being the go-to person for our Italian-speaking customers across the EMEA region, making sure they get an exceptional experience in their own language, while also supporting English-speaking customers day to day.

A day in the life
No two days are the same. You'll be the escalation point for customers and Tier 1 specialists, tackling complex technical and account challenges that demand deeper problem-solving and quick thinking under pressure. When issues require further investigation, you'll collaborate directly with CS Engineering teams to find the right solution. Supporting both English-speaking and Italian-speaking customers, you'll play a vital role in our growing EMEA customer base — ensuring every customer feels heard and supported. It's fast-paced, rewarding, and genuinely impactful.

About the team
At eero, we believe connectivity should simply work — no dead zones, no buffering, no stress. Our Customer Support team is at the heart of that mission, ensuring every customer has a seamless experience from setup to daily use. Based in London, you'll join a collaborative, technically curious team that values knowledge-sharing, continuous improvement, and delivering world-class support. We're growing fast across EMEA, and your bilingual expertise will directly shape how we serve our expanding customer base.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in technical work related to computer systems and technology components
- Experience handling customers and conflict resolution with a focus on quality for customer experience
- Experience in MS Office, with an emphasis on Excel
- Experience in web technologies and the internet
- Experience taking ownership and driving resolution on escalated customer issues
- Experience in technical support, or experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure
- Experience demonstrating strong analytical abilities and confidence in the use of data
- Experience in communicating technically, at a level appropriate for the audience
- Speak, write, and read fluently in Italian and English at B2 level or above
- Ability to identify and troubleshoot technical issues efficiently and logically.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience handling customer escalations
- Knowledge of TCP/IP networks
- Certified Wireless Network Administrator (CWNA) certification (training provided).
- Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) certification (training provided).
- Experience supporting customers across multiple European markets or in a multilingual environment.
